A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LTC-Accel work, with matching methods, experiments, proofs, and qualitative appendices. The added and relocated material supports reliable comparison; a rendering problem in v2 Figure 7 was recoverable from its PDF content.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image and text-to-video experiments, acceleration comparisons, ablations, and convergence analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds AYS comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and a video evaluation using vBench metrics.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects gamma's calculation to use the current step t instead of the fixed cycle r, aligning the inference pseudocode with Equation 6 already present in v1. The transition approximation, weight estimation, and optional refinement otherwise remain unchanged; this correction does not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix D.4 adds video evaluation using WebVid-style prompts, extending the existing COCO-caption coverage to prompts intended for video generation. The PDFs do not identify an actual sampled WebVid dataset. Existing image and video tasks remain.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods are retained. Although v2 Table 2 omits the Original column, the identical 10-step SD v1.5 control and its 0.1111 ImageReward remain in Table 8 for the same experiment. The added AYS budgets use existing comparators, and Anime-diff/Animated-Diff denotes the same cited model.

E3.justification: v2 adds AYS comparisons at 20 versus 15 and 30 versus 20 inference steps, vBench imaging-quality and temporal-flickering metrics, and 40-step hyperparameter sweeps. Existing COCO sample counts, guidance, precision, and evaluation metrics are retained. The single-prompt weight calibration is newly disclosed rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: Figure 7c–d adds targeted 40-step sensitivity tests for acceleration intervals, phi choices, and bias, supplementing the existing convergence, error, bias-PSNR, and skip-step analyses. The original skipping ablation and Table 5 move from Section 4.5 to Appendix A without substantive changes.

E5.justification: The existing prompt-latent counts and shaded variability displays are retained. v2 introduces no new repeated-run or seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds AYS/LTC ImageReward results of 0.1632/0.1510 at 20/15 steps and 0.1901/0.2131 at 30/20 steps. Figure 7 adds video and sensitivity findings; other retained table values are unchanged. Figure 7b plots the 15-step LTC result near 0.170, conflicting with Table 2's 0.1510.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization derivation, and squared-relative-error bound remain unchanged. Equations 1–17 are retained, with the appendix derivations moving from Appendix A to B. The Algorithm 1 correction introduces no new mathematical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the discovery of Local Transition Coherence, architecture-independent training-free acceleration, compatibility claims, and headline speedups. Removing the short conclusion does not remove claims that remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: v2 narrows the tuning limitation from careful hyperparameter tuning generally to primarily choosing acceleration intervals. Appendix D.3 adds an explanation of phi's stabilizing role despite cancellation in the weight product and interprets large thresholds as causing unstable denoising. Appendix D.4 interprets the new video results as preserving perceptual temporal consistency.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 newly states that weights are computed once from a single prompt and reused, describes their overhead as comparable to one forward pass, and recommends tau below 0.15. The abstract now advertises a Colab version through the existing project link. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments changed.

R1.justification: The same 60 bibliography entries are retained. The introduction adds a limited positioning argument that caching methods incur intermediate-feature memory overhead and deployment constraints; the broader related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 relocates the main ablation section to the appendix, separates Limitations, removes the short conclusion, and adds acknowledgements and hyperparameter explanations. Author details and model terminology are edited. Several previously correct Figure 3 references incorrectly become references to Section 2.

P2.justification: v2 adds four-panel Figure 7, restructures Table 2, restyles existing plots, and regroups algorithms and appendix material. The qualitative galleries retain the same examples. Some presentation defects appear: Algorithm 3 overruns the right margin, and Figure 7 contains a problematic line-style command.

improvement.justification: The targeted sensitivity tests, explicit single-prompt weight reuse, and corrected inference pseudocode modestly improve reproducibility and scrutiny of the tuning requirements. Additional video evaluation broadens supporting evidence. These gains are limited by incompletely specified new video sampling, the Table 2/Figure 7b disagreement, and new reference and layout errors; the core scientific contribution remains largely unchanged.
